A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IGPO for multi-turn search-agent reinforcement learning. The main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite revisions and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original IGPO benchmark results, reward-component ablations and training diagnostics for Qwen2.5-3B/7B models.

after.justification: V2 reports revised IGPO experiments and additional reward-design, runtime, reasoning-trace and failure-analysis results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 replace probability differences with differences in mean token log-probability and replace joint normalization of intermediate and outcome rewards with separate normalization. These alter the learning signal. The final F1 reward, discounted accumulation and GRPO-style optimization remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, TQ, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MusiQue, Bamboogle and PopQA for search-based QA. The new trace and failure analyses reuse these benchmarks and introduce no new agent task, domain or search environment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 is unchanged, including the search-agent baselines and RLOO, PPO, GRPO, Reinforce++ and GSPO. Gemini-2.5-pro serves as a diagnostic evaluator; Table 5 introduces within-method design ablations.

E3.justification: Table 4 changes the reported mini-batch size from 32 to 512; the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects reruns or a reporting correction. Appendix D.4 adds a conditional evaluation protocol: select jointly correct answers, remove final answers, and measure teacher reconstruction accuracy from the traces. Runtime profiling is also added.

E4.justification: V2 adds reward-basis and normalization ablations, runtime breakdowns, reasoning-trace informativeness testing, and per-sample degradation analysis with an ambiguous-answer failure example. These substantially expand the questions investigated. The original reward-component ablations and two illustrative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands. The new averages and percentages do not change this practice; reward-normalization standard deviations are algorithmic quantities.

E6.justification: Headline IGPO averages change from 58.7 to 60.2 for 7B and from 47.6 to 48.9 for 3B, with the earlier configuration retained as Prob+Joint in Table 5. The algorithm and reported settings differ. New outcomes include teacher reconstruction accuracies, 3.6% of samples scoring below GRPO, and reported runtime overhead of 0.0227 seconds per step.

T1.justification: The snowball-error definitions, assumptions, theorem and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged apart from numbering. V2 adds a vectorization complexity argument and Appendix F's Transformer FLOP derivation, including an approximate relative-overhead bound below 2g/s when answer length g is much smaller than sequence length s.

C1.justification: The central dense-supervision, accuracy and sample-efficiency claims remain. V2 makes search agents explicit in the title and conclusion and adds negligible computational overhead to its stated contributions. This extends the practical claims without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning reward-scale separation, numerical stability and mitigation of spurious correlations. Appendix E identifies a substantive failure mechanism: ambiguous ground-truth labels can make IGPO penalize valid alternative answers more strongly than GRPO. This substantially extends v1's general limitation concerning ground-truth availability.

D1.justification: V2 adds single-pass attention-mask implementation details, the Gemini evaluator prompt, training-stage timing information and a reproducibility statement, and revises the mini-batch entry. Existing hardware, remaining listed hyperparameters, agent prompt and code URL are retained. These are focused additions to the documented implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Comanici et al. (2025), the Gemini 2.5 reference, for its diagnostic evaluator. Section 5 and the substantive comparison with ReasoningRAG, StepSearch and GiGPO remain unchanged; the latter moves from Appendix D.1 to D.2.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, introduction and motivation, changes advantage terminology to discounted returns, and updates title, author information and conference headers. It adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements and reorganizes the appendices. The main narrative structure and substantial portions of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the training pipeline and adds an attention-mask diagram, runtime plot, evaluator-prompt display and failure-case figure, alongside tables for design variants, timing, trace evaluation and degradation. Existing curves, cases and the agent prompt are relocated or renumbered. The visual explanation and evidence expand substantially beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports its revised design through Table 5 and adds useful implementation, cost and failure evidence absent from v1. The gain is limited by overinterpreting reconstruction from jointly correct traces as evidence against spurious correlations and by new numerical inconsistencies: D.1 calls 47.6 to 48.0 a 0.7-point gain, while D.4's percentage gains disagree with the updated Table 3 it cites. These issues weaken the added conclusions.
